title: Ribbon runs: Threshold file
summary: String runs. Count the numbers in the result list that are at least k (greater than or equal to k).
descriptionMd:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
line is text. A character is one letter, digit, space, or punctuation mark. k is a whole number. Use it as described in the steps below.

Step 1: Build the result list
A run is a group of matching characters next to each other. End a run only when the character changes or the text ends. Record the length of each run, from left to right. Spaces count as characters too. For "aa bb", the result list is [2, 1, 2].

Step 2: Return the answer
Count the numbers in the result list that are at least k (greater than or equal to k). Return that count. An empty list gives 0.

Write your function
Complete ribbonRunsThresholdFile(line, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.
unitIntro: A run is a group of matching characters next to each other. End a run only when the character changes or the text ends. Record the length of each run, from left to right. Spaces count as characters too. For "aa bb", the result list is [2, 1, 2]. Each card first builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.
constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
The text uses ASCII characters (a basic character set). Only an ordinary space separates words.
Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the result list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
hints: Try a small example by hand. Follow Step 1 and write down its result list.

A run is a group of matching characters next to each other. End a run only when the character changes or the text ends. Record the length of each run, from left to right. Spaces count as characters too. For "aa bb", the result list is [2, 1, 2]. Keep track of the numbers or places you have already checked.
Count the numbers in the result list that are at least k (greater than or equal to k). Return that count. An empty list gives 0. Check what to do if the result list is empty.

cases.explanation: Step 1 gives the result list [1,1,2,1,1,3,1,1,1]. Here k = 3. The numbers at least 3 are [3]. There are 1, so return 1.
Step 1 gives the result list [2,1,1,2]. Here k = 2. The numbers at least 2 are [2,2]. There are 2, so return 2.
Step 1 gives the result list []. Here k = 1. The numbers at least 1 are []. There are 0, so return 0.

overview: The two steps ask different things: first build a list, then return the answer requested. Follow the order, keep repeated values when required, and check the empty case.
